messages.content: We settled on Gulf Shores for March 10 through March 15, so I want to finish the lodging comparison. It is still two adults and our 14-year-old. The finalists are the beachfront hotel and the one-bedroom condo. Can you verify that both really sleep three and put every required charge into a five-night total?

Yes. Send me the current rate and fee details from each listing, including any deposit and cancellation language. I will separate mandatory lodging costs from refundable holds so the totals are comparable.

The hotel shows a two-queen room at $289 per night. It also says $35 nightly resort fee, $22 nightly parking, and estimated taxes of $214.20. The room page says maximum occupancy four. I cannot tell whether the resort fee is already inside the displayed room total.

On those figures, the hotel calculation is: $1,445 room charge for five nights, $175 resort fee, $110 parking, and $214.20 tax. That produces a mandatory total of $1,944.20. I am treating the resort fee as additional because the listing describes it as a nightly charge rather than part of the $289 rate. The checkout page still needs to confirm that it is not counted twice.

The bedding line says two queen beds, no rollaway, and three registered guests are allowed. It also says breakfast buffet included for registered guests. If that really covers all three of us, count it in the hotel's favor. I prefer hotels that include breakfast when there is a workable choice, especially when we need to get moving in the morning.

The sleeping arrangement works without an extra bed: two queen beds and an occupancy limit of four cover three registered guests. I will count breakfast as an advantage, but not assign it a dollar value until the rate details confirm that the included buffet applies to two adults and the 14-year-old rather than only two guests.

For the condo, the base rate is $270 a night. There is a $225 cleaning fee, a $145 service fee, and $187.20 in taxes. Parking for one car is included. It has one king bedroom and a queen sleeper sofa in the living room.

The condo mandatory total is $1,907.20: $1,350 for five nights, plus $225 cleaning, $145 service fee, and $187.20 tax. That is $37 less than the hotel. The king bed plus queen sleeper sofa can sleep three, provided the condo's occupancy rules allow the 14-year-old and the sleeper sofa includes linens.
I found that section. Maximum occupancy is four, children are allowed, and sheets and pillows for the sleeper sofa are included. There is also a $300 damage deposit. Is that part of the $1,907.20?

Not if it is a refundable damage deposit collected separately. It should be shown as $1,907.20 in mandatory trip cost plus a temporary $300 cash-flow requirement. If the owner can retain any portion as a nonrefundable damage waiver or processing fee, that portion belongs in the mandatory total.
It says a $300 card authorization is placed two days before arrival and released within seven days after checkout if there is no damage. No damage-waiver fee is listed.

Then the comparable condo total remains $1,907.20. The $300 is a separate refundable authorization, not part of the lodging cost, though you need enough available credit for it around March 8 through as late as March 22.

Now the payment and cancellation terms. The hotel charges one night plus tax when booked. It is refundable if canceled by 6:00 p.m. Central on February 24. After that, the deposit is forfeited. The rest is due at the property.

Using the tax proportion in the quote, the estimated hotel booking deposit is about $331.84: one $289 night, about $42.84 allocated tax, with the resort fee and parking apparently payable at the property. The exact deposit must come from checkout. The important point is that the deposit remains recoverable through February 24 at 6:00 p.m. Central; a later cancellation costs that deposit rather than the full stay, assuming the terms contain no separate no-show penalty.

The condo takes 50% of the complete rental amount now and the other 50% on February 9. Cancellation is a full refund minus a $75 administrative fee through January 31, a 50% refund from February 1 through February 15, and no refund after February 15.

That means two condo payments of $953.60. Its cancellation protection is materially weaker: even an early cancellation costs $75, cancellation from February 1 through 15 could leave $953.60 unrecovered, and after February 15 the full $1,907.20 is at risk. The hotel preserves a full deposit refund until February 24 and exposes much less money after that deadline.
Both totals are under the $2,000 lodging cap, correct? Do not count the refundable condo authorization against the cap.
Correct. The hotel is $1,944.20, which is $55.80 under the cap. The condo is $1,907.20, which is $92.80 under. Excluding the refundable authorization, the condo has $37 more room under the cap.

The condo's separate living room would be useful because our daughter would not have to go to sleep on the same schedule we do. Is that enough to outweigh the cancellation issue and the hotel breakfast?

It is the condo's strongest advantage. You gain a closed bedroom, a separate living area, and $37 in savings. In exchange, your daughter sleeps on a sofa bed, you accept a $300 authorization, and substantially more money becomes nonrefundable earlier. The hotel gives everyone a standard bed, includes breakfast if the rate covers all three guests, and has the more forgiving cancellation deadline. With only a $37 price gap, the hotel offers the stronger overall value unless the separate room is essential for this stay.
It is helpful, not essential. Make the final choice, but list the exact items that still need confirmation before I book.

Choose the beachfront hotel. Its $1,944.20 working mandatory total is only $37 above the condo, stays within the $2,000 cap, provides two queen beds for three registered guests, and has much better cancellation protection. The included breakfast also offsets some of that small price difference if it applies to the whole party. Before booking, verify that checkout shows two adults and one 14-year-old for March 10-15; two queen beds and occupancy for three; $1,445 room charge; $175 resort fee; $110 parking for one car; $214.20 tax; and a final mandatory total of $1,944.20. Confirm that buffet breakfast is included for all three registered guests, the exact advance deposit, full deposit refund through February 24 at 6:00 p.m. Central, and any incidental hold at check-in. Nothing has been booked.
